rv.q: Cleverly conceived—and often sharply funny—'Trophy Boys' nevertheless often feels like a debate itself, with Ms. Mattana expounding upon various ideas about the current discourse around gender and the reverberations of the #MeToo movement, sometimes at eye-glazing length.
But then she bottles the thing up neatly with another few swivels of plot.
I can say that it doesn’t make a winning argument: The two characterizations nullify each other, leaving the audience to shrug.
It’s a juicy setup steeped in satire, and the playwright doubles down by flipping the script on gender.
Mattana offers an eye-opening look at the rising ruling class of this country on the eve of its 249th birthday in Trophy Boys, now making its US premiere at MCC Theater.
Trophy Boys certainly excels in exposing the performative contradictions of male allyship
Mattana has set up a wonderful premise, but then doesn’t quite know where to take it.
Taymor’s production is a humorous, stiff-upper-lipped response to repressive times.

cn.t: Critics find this sharp 70-minute satire of elite prep school culture clever and provocative, particularly its gender-flipped casting, though some question whether its ambitious takedown of privilege fully connects.
